# Toyota Hiace (2012) - Repair Procedures: Engine & Drivetrain

> **Source:** Toyota Workshop Manual | **Section:** Repair Procedures: Engine & Drivetrain

---

### GENERATOR > DISASSEMBLY

GENERATOR > DISASSEMBLY
for Preparation
Click here
1. REMOVE GENERATOR WITH CLUTCH PULLEY
Remove the generator pulley cap.
Install SST to the pulley and vise as shown in the illustration.
SST
09820-63020
Mount SST (A) in a vise.
Turn SST (B) clockwise, and loosen the pulley.
Remove the pulley.
2. REMOVE GENERATOR REAR END COVER
Remove the 3 nuts and generator rear end cover.
3. REMOVE TERMINAL INSULATOR
Remove the terminal insulator.
4. REMOVE GENERATOR BRUSH HOLDER ASSEMBLY
Remove the 2 screws and generator brush holder assembly.
5. REMOVE GENERATOR COIL ASSEMBLY
Remove the 4 through bolts.
Using SST, remove the generator coil.
SST
09950-40011
(09951-04020, 09952-04010, 09953-04020, 09954-04010, 09955-04071, 09957-04010, 09958-04011)
Remove the generator washer.
6. REMOVE GENERATOR ROTOR ASSEMBLY
Remove the generator rotor from the drive end frame.
7. INSPECT GENERATOR DRIVE END FRAME BEARING
Inspect than the bearing is not rough or worn. If necessary, replace the bearing.
8. REMOVE GENERATOR DRIVE END FRAME BEARING
Remove the 4 screws and bearing retainer.
Using SST, tap out the bearing.
SST
09950-60010
(09951-00250)
09950-70010
(09951-07100)

### GENERATOR > REASSEMBLY

GENERATOR > REASSEMBLY
for Preparation
Click here
1. INSTALL GENERATOR DRIVE END FRAME BEARING
Using SST and a press, press in a new bearing.
SST
09950-60010
(09951-00470)
09950-70010
(09951-07100)
Align the claws of the bearing retainer with the grooves inside the drive end frame.
Install the bearing retainer with the 4 screws.
2. INSTALL GENERATOR ROTOR ASSEMBLY
Install the rotor and washer to the drive end frame.
3. INSTALL GENERATOR COIL ASSEMBLY
Using deep socket wrench (21 mm) and a press, slowly press in the generator coil assembly.
Install the generator coil assembly with the 4 through bolts.
Torque:
5.8 N*m{
59 kgf*cm
, 51 in.*lbf
}
4. INSTALL GENERATOR BRUSH HOLDER ASSEMBLY
While pushing the 2 brushes to the inside of the generator brush holder assembly, insert a φ1.0 mm (0.039 in.) pin into the generator brush holder hole.
Install the brush holder assembly with the 2 screws.
Pull out the pin from the brush holder assembly.
5. INSTALL TERMINAL INSULATOR
Install the terminal insulator.
6. INSTALL GENERATOR REAR END COVER
Install the generator rear end cover with the 3 nuts.
Torque:
4.6 N*m{
47 kgf*cm
, 41 in.*lbf
}
7. INSTALL GENERATOR WITH CLUTCH PULLEY
Install the pulley by hand.
Install SST to the pulley and vise as shown in the illustration.
SST
09820-63020
Turn SST (B) counterclockwise, and tighten the pulley.
SST
09820-63020
Torque:
87 N*m{
891 kgf*cm
, 64 ft.*lbf
}
NOTICE:
Use a torque wrench with a fulcrum length of 380 mm (14.96 in.).
Check that the generator pulley rotates smoothly.
Install the generator pulley cap.

### STARTER (for 2.0 kW Type) > DISASSEMBLY

STARTER (for 2.0 kW Type) > DISASSEMBLY
for Preparation
Click here
1. REMOVE STARTER YOKE ASSEMBLY
Remove the nut, then disconnect the lead wire from terminal C.
Remove the 2 through bolts, then pull starter yoke and starter armature.
Remove the O-ring from the starter yoke.
2. REMOVE MAGNET STARTER SWITCH ASSEMBLY
Remove the 2 screws, then remove the magnet starter switch.
Remove the starter clutch from the starter drive housing.
Remove the magnet switch return spring from the starter clutch.
Remove the starter idle pinion from the starter drive housing.
Remove the retainer from the starter drive housing.
Remove the clutch roller from the retainer.
Remove the pinion gear from the starter drive housing.
Using a magnetic finger, remove the steel ball from the starter clutch.
3. REMOVE STARTER BRUSH HOLDER ASSEMBLY
Remove the 2 screws, then remove the commutator end frame from the starter yoke.
Remove the dust protector from the commutator end frame.
Remove the O-ring from the starter yoke.
Using a screwdriver, hold the spring back and disconnect the 4 brushes from the brush holder.
Remove the brush holder from the starter armature.
4. REMOVE STARTER ARMATURE ASSEMBLY
Remove the starter armature from the starter yoke.

---

### STARTER (for 2.2 kW Type) > DISASSEMBLY

STARTER (for 2.2 kW Type) > DISASSEMBLY
for Preparation
Click here
1. REMOVE STARTER YOKE ASSEMBLY
Remove the nut and disconnect the lead wire from terminal C.
Remove the 2 bolts.
Pull out the starter yoke with the armature.
Remove the O-ring from the starter yoke assembly.
2. REMOVE MAGNET STARTER SWITCH ASSEMBLY
Remove the 2 screws and magnet starter switch.
Remove the return spring, pinion gear, idler gear, clutch roller, retainer and starter clutch from the starter housing.
Using a magnetic finger, remove the steel ball from the clutch shaft hole.
3. REMOVE STARTER BRUSH HOLDER ASSEMBLY
Disconnect the 4 starter yoke brushes from the brush holder.
Using a screwdriver, pull back the spring.
Disconnect the brush from the brush holder.
Remove the brush holder assembly from the starter yoke assembly.
4. REMOVE STARTER ARMATURE ASSEMBLY
Using a plastic-faced hammer, tap the frame end to remove the starter armature assembly from the starter yoke assembly.

### STARTER (for 1.4 kW Type) > DISASSEMBLY

STARTER (for 1.4 kW Type) > DISASSEMBLY
for Preparation
Click here
1. REMOVE STARTER YOKE ASSEMBLY
Remove the nut, and then disconnect the lead wire from terminal C.
Remove the 2 through bolts.
Pull out the starter yoke together with the starter armature.
Remove the O-ring from the starter yoke.
2. REMOVE MAGNET STARTER SWITCH ASSEMBLY
Remove the 2 screws and magnet starter switch.
Remove the idle gear, retainer, clutch roller, return spring and starter clutch from the starter drive housing.
Using a magnet hand, remove the steel ball from the starter clutch.
3. REMOVE STARTER BRUSH HOLDER ASSEMBLY
Remove the 2 screws and commutator end frame from the starter yoke.
Remove the dust starter protector from the commutator end frame.
Remove the O-ring from the starter yoke.
Disconnect the 4 brushes from the starter brush holder.
Using a screwdriver, hold back the brush spring.
Disconnect the brush from the brush holder.
Remove the brush holder from the starter armature.
4. REMOVE STARTER ARMATURE ASSEMBLY
Remove the starter armature from the starter yoke.

### STARTER (for 2.0 kW Type) > REASSEMBLY

STARTER (for 2.0 kW Type) > REASSEMBLY
for Preparation
Click here
1. INSTALL STARTER ARMATURE ASSEMBLY
Install the starter armature to the starter yoke.
2. INSTALL STARTER BRUSH HOLDER ASSEMBLY
Place the brush holder assembly on the starter yoke.
Using a screwdriver, install the 4 brushes.
NOTICE:
Check that the positive (+) lead wires are not grounded.
Place a new O-ring in position on the commutator end frame.
Install the new dust protector to the commutator end frame.
Install the commutator end frame with the 2 screws.
Torque:
3.8 N*m{
39 kgf*cm
, 34 in.*lbf
}
3. INSTALL MAGNET STARTER SWITCH ASSEMBLY
Apply grease to the steel ball and install it onto the starter clutch.
Apply grease to the starter clutch, and install it onto the starter drive housing.
Apply grease to the magnet switch return spring and install it onto the starter clutch.
Apply grease to the clutch roller and install it onto the retainer.
Apply grease to the retainer and install it onto the starter idle pinion.
Apply grease to the starter idle pinion and install it onto the starter drive housing.
Apply grease to the pinion gear and install it onto the starter drive housing.
Install the starter switch with the 2 screws.
Torque:
9.3 N*m{
95 kgf*cm
, 82 in.*lbf
}
4. INSTALL STARTER YOKE ASSEMBLY
Place a new O-ring in position on the starter yoke.
Install the starter yoke to the starter switch.
HINT:
Align the claw of the starter yoke with the groove of the starter switch.
Tighten the 2 through bolts.
Torque:
9.3 N*m{
95 kgf*cm
, 82 in.*lbf
}
Connect the lead wire to terminal C with the nut.
Torque:
5.9 N*m{
60 kgf*cm
, 52 in.*lbf
}

### STARTER (for 2.2 kW Type) > REASSEMBLY

STARTER (for 2.2 kW Type) > REASSEMBLY
for Preparation
Click here
1. INSTALL STARTER CLUTCH ASSEMBLY
Apply grease to the steel ball, return spring, clutch roller, retainer, pinion gear and idler gear.
Install the steel ball.
Insert the return spring into the starter clutch hole.
Install the starter clutch, idler gear, pinion gear, retainer and clutch roller.
Install the starter housing to the magnet switch with the 2 screws.
Torque:
9.3 N*m{
95 kgf*cm
, 82 in.*lbf
}
2. INSTALL STARTER ARMATURE ASSEMBLY
Apply grease to the starter armature bearing.
Using a press, press the starter armature into the starter yoke assembly.
3. INSTALL STARTER BRUSH HOLDER ASSEMBLY
Align the claw of the brush holder with the claw groove of the starter yoke assembly.
Place the brush holder on the starter yoke assembly.
Install the 4 starter yoke brushes to the brush holder.
Using a screwdriver, pull back the spring.
Install the brush to the brush holder.
NOTICE:
Check that the positive (+) lead wires are not grounded.
4. INSTALL STARTER YOKE ASSEMBLY
Install a new O-ring to the groove of the starter yoke assembly.
Align the claws of the starter brush holder with the grooves of the magnet starter switch, and install the starter yoke assembly and starter armature assembly.
Align the punch mark of the starter yoke with the line of the magnet starter switch assembly.
Install 2 new O-rings to the bolts.
Install the starter yoke with the 2 bolts.
Torque:
13 N*m{
130 kgf*cm
, 9 ft.*lbf
}
Connect the lead wire to terminal C with the nut.
Torque:
5.9 N*m{
60 kgf*cm
, 52 in.*lbf
}

### STARTER (for 1.6 kW Type) > DISASSEMBLY

STARTER (for 1.6 kW Type) > DISASSEMBLY
for Preparation
Click here
1. REMOVE REPAIR SERVICE STARTER KIT
Remove the nut, and disconnect the lead wire from terminal C.
Remove the 2 screws that holds the repair service starter kit from the starter drive housing.
Remove the repair service starter kit.
2. REMOVE STARTER YOKE ASSEMBLY
Remove the 2 through bolts, and pull out the starter yoke assembly together with the starter commutator end frame assembly.
3. REMOVE STARTER COMMUTATOR END FRAME ASSEMBLY
Remove the starter commutator end frame assembly from the starter yoke.
4. REMOVE STARTER ARMATURE PLATE
Remove the starter armature plate from the starter yoke.
5. REMOVE STARTER COMMUTATOR END FRAME COVER
Using a screwdriver, remove the starter commutator end frame cover.
6. REMOVE STARTER ARMATURE ASSEMBLY
Hold the starter commutator end frame in a vise between aluminum plates.
Using snap ring pliers, remove the snap ring and plate washer.
Remove the starter armature assembly from the commutator end frame.
7. REMOVE PLANET GEAR
Remove the 3 planet gears.
8. REMOVE STARTER CENTER BEARING CLUTCH SUB-ASSEMBLY
Remove the starter center bearing clutch sub-assembly with the starter drive lever set pin from the starter drive housing.
Remove the starter drive lever set pin from the starter center bearing clutch sub-assembly.

---

### STARTER (for 1.6 kW Type) > REASSEMBLY

STARTER (for 1.6 kW Type) > REASSEMBLY
for Preparation
Click here
1. INSTALL STARTER CENTER BEARING CLUTCH SUB-ASSEMBLY
Install the drive lever set pin to the starter center bearing clutch sub-assembly
Install the starter center bearing clutch with the drive lever set pin to the starter drive housing.
2. INSTALL PLANET GEAR
Apply grease to the planet gears and pin parts of the planet shaft.
Install the 3 planet gears.
3. INSTALL STARTER ARMATURE ASSEMBLY
Apply grease to the plate washer and armature shaft.
Install the armature shaft to the starter commutator end frame.
Using snap ring pliers, install the plate washer and a new snap ring.
NOTICE:
Be sure to install the snap ring in the armature shaft groove securely.
Be sure to properly install the snap ring because it easily expands.
Using vernier calipers, measure the snap ring.
Maximum length:
5.0 mm (0.197 in.)
If the length is greater than the maximum, replace the snap ring.
4. INSTALL STARTER COMMUTATOR END FRAME COVER
Install the starter commutator end frame cover to the starter commutator end frame.
5. INSTALL STARTER ARMATURE PLATE
Align the claw of the armature plate with the groove inside the starter yoke, and install the starter armature plate.
6. INSTALL STARTER COMMUTATOR END FRAME ASSEMBLY
Align the starter commutator end frame rubber with the groove of the starter yoke.
Install the starter commutator end frame to the starter yoke.
NOTICE:
The magnet of the starter yoke may attract the starter armature when the starter commutator end frame is installed, causing the magnet break.
7. INSTALL STARTER YOKE ASSEMBLY
Align the claw of the starter yoke assembly with the groove inside the starter drive housing.
Install the starter yoke assembly with the 2 bolts.
Torque:
6.0 N*m{
61 kgf*cm
, 53 in.*lbf
}
8. INSTALL REPAIR SERVICE STARTER KIT
Apply grease to the plunger and hook.
Hang the plunger hook of the repair service starter kit to the drive lever.
Install the repair service starter kit with the 2 screws.
Torque:
7.5 N*m{
77 kgf*cm
, 66 in.*lbf
}
Connect the lead wire to terminal C with the nut.
Torque:
10 N*m{
102 kgf*cm
, 7 ft.*lbf
}

### GENERATOR > DISASSEMBLY

GENERATOR > DISASSEMBLY
for Preparation
Click here
1. REMOVE GENERATOR WITH CLUTCH PULLEY (w/ Clutch Pulley)
Using a screwdriver, remove the generator pulley cap from the generator with clutch pulley.
Mount the generator in a vise between aluminum plates.
Install SST (A) and SST (B) to the generator with clutch pulley as shown in the illustration.
SST
09820-63020
NOTICE:
Securely attach SST to the generator with clutch pulley and generator rotor shaft.
Use a wrench to hold SST (A) and turn SST (B) counterclockwise to loosen the generator with clutch pulley.
NOTICE:
Be careful as the generator with clutch pulley or generator rotor shaft may be damaged if the position of SST is not securely maintained while performing this operation.
Remove SST from the generator.
Remove the generator with clutch pulley from the rotor shaft.
2. REMOVE GENERATOR PULLEY (w/o Clutch Pulley)
Install SST (1-A) to the pulley shaft.
SST
09820-63010
(09820-06010, 09820-06020)
HINT:
SST (1-A) and (1-B)
09820-06010
SST 2
09820-06020
Install SST (1-B) to SST (1-A).
Hold SST (1-A) with a torque wrench, and tighten SST (1-B) clockwise with the specified torque.
Torque:
39 N*m{
400 kgf*cm
, 29 ft.*lbf
}
NOTICE:
Check that SST is secured to the generator rotor shaft.
Mount the generator in a vise between aluminum plates.
Insert SST 2 and attach it to the pulley nut.
To loosen the pulley nut, turn SST (1-A) in the direction shown in the illustration.
NOTICE:
To prevent damage to the rotor shaft, do not loosen the pulley nut more than one-half turn.
Remove SST 2 from the generator.
Turn SST (1-A), and remove SST (1-A) and (1-B).
Remove the generator pulley nut and generator pulley.
3. REMOVE GENERATOR REAR END COVER
Remove the 3 nuts and generator rear end cover.
4. REMOVE TERMINAL INSULATOR
Remove the terminal insulator.
5. REMOVE GENERATOR BRUSH HOLDER ASSEMBLY
Remove the 2 screws and generator brush holder assembly.
6. REMOVE GENERATOR COIL ASSEMBLY
Remove the 4 through bolts.
Using SST, remove the generator coil assembly.
SST
09950-40011
(09951-04020, 09952-04010, 09953-04020, 09954-04010, 09955-04071, 09957-04010, 09958-04011)
7. REMOVE GENERATOR ROTOR ASSEMBLY
Remove the generator washer.
Remove the generator rotor assembly from the generator rear end cover.
8. INSPECT GENERATOR DRIVE END FRAME BEARING
Check that the generator drive end frame bearing is not rough or worn.
If necessary, replace the generator drive end frame bearing.
9. REMOVE GENERATOR DRIVE END FRAME BEARING
Remove the 4 screws and bearing retainer.
Using SST and a hammer, tap out the generator drive end frame bearing.
SST
09950-60010
(09951-00250)
09950-70010
(09951-07100)

### DIFFERENTIAL OIL > ADJUSTMENT

DIFFERENTIAL OIL > ADJUSTMENT
for Preparation
Click here
1. INSPECT AND ADJUST DIFFERENTIAL OIL
Stop the vehicle on a level place.
Remove the differential filler plug and gasket.
Check that the oil surface is within 5 mm (0.20 in.) of the lowest position of the inner surface of the differential filler plug opening.
NOTICE:
Excessively large or small amounts of oil may cause trouble.
After replacing oil, drive the vehicle and check the oil level.
HINT:
If necessary, fill the rear differential carrier with hypoid gear oil.
Check for oil leakage when the oil level is low.
Install the differential filler plug and a new gasket.
Torque:
49 N*m{
500 kgf*cm
, 36 ft.*lbf
}
2. FILL DIFFERENTIAL OIL
Remove the differential filler plug and gasket.
Fill with oil.
Oil grade:
Hypoid gear oil API GL-5 or equivalent
Recommended oil viscosity
Above -18°C (0°F)
SAE 90
Below -18°C (0°F)
SAE 80W or 80W-90
Check the oil level.
Install the differential filler plug with a new gasket.
Torque:
49 N*m{
500 kgf*cm
, 36 ft.*lbf
}
NOTICE:
After replacing the oil, recheck the oil level after driving.

### DIFFERENTIAL SYSTEM > PRECAUTION

DIFFERENTIAL SYSTEM > PRECAUTION
for Preparation
Click here
1.Before disassembly, clean the outside of the differential assembly and remove any sand or mud to prevent it from entering the inside of the assembly during disassembly and installation.
2.When removing a connected part made of light alloy such as a differential carrier cover, tap it off with a plastic hammer. Do not attempt to pry it off with a screwdriver.
3.Always arrange disassembled parts in order and protect them from dust.
4.Before installation, thoroughly clean and dry each part and then apply hypoid gear oil API GL-5 or equivalent to them. Do not use alkaline cleaner for aluminum or rubber parts and ring gear set bolts. Also, do not clean rubber parts such as O-rings or oil seals with white gasoline.
5.Coat any sliding surface and rotating part with hypoid gear oil API GL-5 or equivalent.
6.When holding a part with a vise, be sure to place an aluminum sheet between the part and vise. Do not put it directly in the vise.
7.Do not damage the contact surfaces of the case. Such damage may cause oil leakage.
8.Do not fill with oil immediately after installing sealed parts. Wait at least an hour.
9.Damage to the surfaces being contact with an oil seal, O-ring or gasket may cause oil leakage.
10.When press-fitting an oil seal, do not damage the oil seal lip or outside periphery.
11.When replacing a bearing, replace the inner and outer races as a set.

### CLUTCH UNIT (for 5L-E) > INSTALLATION

CLUTCH UNIT (for 5L-E) > INSTALLATION
for Preparation
Click here
1. INSTALL INPUT SHAFT BEARING
Using SST and a hammer, install a new input shaft bearing.
SST
09304-12012
Install the 2 bolts.
Torque:
123 N*m{
1,250 kgf*cm
, 90 ft.*lbf
}
2. INSTALL CLUTCH DISC ASSEMBLY
Insert SST into the clutch disc assembly, then insert them into the flywheel sub-assembly.
SST
09301-00110
NOTICE:
Take care not to insert the clutch disc assembly in the wrong direction.
3. INSTALL CLUTCH COVER ASSEMBLY
Align the matchmarks on the clutch cover assembly with the one on the flywheel sub-assembly.
Following the procedures shown in the illustration, tighten the 6 bolts starting from the bolt located near the knock pin on the top.
SST
09301-00110
Torque:
19 N*m{
195 kgf*cm
, 14 ft.*lbf
}
HINT:
Evenly tighten the bolts by following the order shown in the illustration.
Tighten the bolts after checking that the disc is in the center by lightly moving the SST up and down, left and right.
4. INSPECT AND ADJUST CLUTCH COVER ASSEMBLY
Using a dial indicator with a roller instrument, check the diaphragm spring tip alignment.
Maximum non-alignment:
0.9 mm (0.035 in.)
If alignment is not as specified, adjust the diaphragm spring tip alignment using SST.
SST
09333-00013
5. INSTALL CLUTCH RELEASE FORK BOOT
Install the clutch release fork boot.
6. INSTALL RELEASE FORK SUPPORT
Install the clutch release fork support to the transmission unit.
Torque:
39 N*m{
400 kgf*cm
, 29 ft.*lbf
}
7. INSTALL CLUTCH RELEASE FORK SUB-ASSEMBLY
Apply Multemp 8158 Grease or equivalent to the release fork, the release bearing assembly, the push rod contact point and the pivot points as shown in the illustration.
Grease:
Multemp 8158 Grease or equivalent
Apply clutch spline grease to the input shaft spline.
Sealant:
Toyota Genuine Clutch Spline Grease or equivalent
Install the release bearing to the clutch release fork with the clip.
Install the clutch release fork assembly to the transmission unit.
NOTICE:
After installation, move the fork back and forth to check that the release bearing slides smoothly.
8. INSTALL MANUAL TRANSMISSION UNIT ASSEMBLY
(
Click here
)

CLUTCH UNIT (for 5L-E) > REMOVAL
for Preparation
Click here
1. REMOVE MANUAL TRANSMISSION UNIT ASSEMBLY
(
Click here

2. REMOVE CLUTCH RELEASE FORK SUB-ASSEMBLY

Remove the clutch release fork boot from the transmission unit.
4. REMOVE RELEASE FORK SUPPORT
Remove the release fork support from the transmission unit.
5. REMOVE CLUTCH COVER ASSEMBLY
Put matchmarks on the clutch cover assembly and the flywheel sub-assembly.
Loosen each set bolt one turn at a time until spring tension is released.
NOTICE:
Do not drop the clutch disc assembly.
Remove the set bolts, and pull off the clutch cover assembly.
6. REMOVE CLUTCH DISC ASSEMBLY
NOTICE:
Keep the lining part of the clutch disc assembly, the pressure plate and surface of the flywheel sub-assembly away from oil and foreign matter.
7. INSPECT INPUT SHAFT BEARING
Turn the bearing by hand while applying force in the direction of the rotation.
HINT:
The bearing is permanently lubricated and requires no cleaning or lubrication.
8. REMOVE INPUT SHAFT BEARING
Remove the 2 bolts at symmetrically opposite points.
Using SST, remove the input shaft bearing.
SST
09303-35011

### PROPELLER SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Long Wheelbase) > REMOVAL

PROPELLER SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Long Wheelbase) > REMOVAL
for Preparation
Click here
1. REMOVE PROPELLER SHAFT ASSEMBLY
Put matchmarks on both flanges.
Remove the 4 nuts, bolts and washers.
HINT:
If the flange connection is hard to separate, temporarily tighten one nut only and evenly tap the flange with a brass bar and hammer to separate the propeller shaft assembly from the differential companion flange.
Remove the propeller shaft assembly.
Insert SST in the transmission to prevent oil leakage.
NOTICE:
Do not damage the oil seal.
Use the following SST for the automatic transmission
SST
09325-40010
Use the following SST for the manual transmission
SST
09325-20010
2. INSPECT PROPELLER SHAFT ASSEMBLY
Visually check the propeller shaft assembly.
Using a dial indicator, inspect the runout of the shaft tube.
Runout of propeller shaft:
Shaft tube length mm (in.)
Maximum runout mm (in.)
800 (31.496) or more
0.4 (0.0157)
Less than 800 (31.496)
0.3 (0.0118)
3. INSPECT UNIVERSAL JOINT SPIDER ASSEMBLY
Check that the spider bearing rotates smoothly.
Check that there is no play in the spider bearing.
Using a spring tension gauge, hang the hook of the spring tension gauge on the bolt hole of the flange yoke and measure the rotating force.
Maximum:
1.1 N*m (11.2 kgf*cm, 9.68 in.*lbf)
NOTICE:
Measurement of rotating force should be done at 2 positions for each universal joint by 90° in opposite directions (flange yoke side and end yoke side). When the rotating force is less than the standard, use a thicker retainer ring. When it exceeds the standard, use a thinner one.

### PROPELLER SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Long Wheelbase) > DISASSEMBLY

PROPELLER SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Long Wheelbase) > DISASSEMBLY
for Preparation
Click here
1. REMOVE UNIVERSAL JOINT SPIDER ASSEMBLY
Put matchmarks on the flange yoke and propeller shaft assembly.
Using a brass bar and a hammer, slightly tap in the spider bearing outer races.
Using 2 screwdrivers, remove the 4 snap rings from the grooves.
Hold the propeller shaft assembly in a vise between aluminium plates.
NOTICE:
Do not overtighten the vise.
Using SST, push out the spider bearing from the propeller shaft.
SST
09332-25010
HINT:
Sufficiently raise the part indicated by (A) so that it does not come into contact with the spider bearing.
Clamp the spider bearing outer race in a vise between aluminium plates and tap off the propeller shaft with a hammer.
NOTICE:
Do not overtighten the vise.
Do not tap the shaft.
HINT:
Remove the spider bearing on the opposite side using the same procedure.
Install the 2 removed spider bearing outer races to the spider.
Hold the flange yoke in a vise between aluminium plates.
NOTICE:
Do not overtighten the vise.
Using SST, push out the spider bearing from the flange yoke.
SST
09332-25010
HINT:
Sufficiently raise the part indicated by (A) so that it does not come into contact with the spider bearing.
Clamp the spider bearing outer race in a vise between aluminium plates and tap off the propeller shaft with a hammer.
NOTICE:
Do not overtighten the vise.
Do not damage the flange yoke.
Remove the universal joint spider.
HINT:
Remove the spider bearing on the opposite side using the same procedure.

### AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION FLUID > INSPECTION

AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION FLUID > INSPECTION
for Preparation
Click here
1. INSPECT AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION FLUID LEVEL
HINT:
Drive the vehicle so that the engine and transmission are at normal operating temperature.
Fluid temperature:
70 to 80 °C (158 to 176 °F)
Park the vehicle on a level surface and set the parking brake.
With the engine idling and the brake pedal depressed, move shift the lever into all positions from P to L and return to the P position.
Take out the dipstick and wipe it clean.
Put it back all the way.
Take it out again and check that the fluid level is within the HOT range.
If the fluid level is below the HOT range, add new fluid and recheck the fluid level. If the fluid level exceeds the HOT range, drain the fluid once, add the proper amount of new fluid and recheck the fluid level.

### MANUAL TRANSMISSION EXTENSION HOUSING OIL SEAL > INSTALLATION

MANUAL TRANSMISSION EXTENSION HOUSING OIL SEAL > INSTALLATION
for Preparation
Click here
1. INSTALL MANUAL TRANSMISSION EXTENSION HOUSING OIL SEAL
Using SST and a hammer, install a new oil seal to the extension housing.
SST
09325-20010
Drive in depth:
- 0.5 to 0.5 mm (-0.020 to 0.020 in.)
Coat the lip of the oil seal with MP grease.
2. INSTALL PROPELLER SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Long Wheelbase)
Remove the SST from the extension housing.
Install the propeller shaft assembly in the extension housing.
Align the matchmarks on the propeller shaft flange and differential flange.
Install the propeller shaft assembly with the 4 nuts, 4 bolts and 4 washers.
Torque:
74 N*m{
755 kgf*cm
, 54 ft.*lbf
}
3. INSTALL PROPELLER WITH CENTER BEARING SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Super Long Wheelbase)
Remove the SST from the extension housing.
Install the propeller with center bearing shaft assembly in the extension housing.
Install the center support bearing assembly No.1, and temporarily tighten the 2 bolts.
Align the matchmarks on the propeller shaft flange and differential flange.
Install the propeller shaft assembly with the 4 nuts, 4 bolts and 4 washers.
Torque:
74 N*m{
755 kgf*cm
, 54 ft.*lbf
}
Check that the center line of the bracket is at right angles to the shaft axial direction.
Adjust the center support bearing assembly No.1.
HINT:
With the vehicle unladen, adjust the center support bearing No.1 to maintain the angles, as shown.
In the same conditions, check the center line in the axial direction. Adjust the bearing if necessary.
The center bearing center line and center bearing housing center line must be adjusted to within -1.0 to 1.0 mm (-0.0394 to 0.0394 in.) of each other in the vehicle's longitudinal direction with the vehicle unladen.
Tighten the 2 bolts.
Torque:
36 N*m{
369 kgf*cm
, 27 ft.*lbf
}
4. ADD MANUAL TRANSMISSION OIL
Park the vehicle in a level place.
Remove the transmission filler plug and gasket.
Check that the oil surface is within 5 mm (0.20 in.) below the lowest point of the transmission filler plug opening.
Oil grade:
GL-4 or GL-5
Viscosity:
SAE 75W-90
Capacity:
2.2 liters (2.3 US qts, 1.9 lmp. qts)
NOTICE:
Problems may occur when the oil level is too high or too low.
After replacing the oil, drive the vehicle and check the oil level again.
Check for oil leakage if the oil level is low.
Install the transmission filler plug and a new gasket.
Torque:
37 N*m{
377 kgf*cm
, 27 ft.*lbf
}

Remove the 2 bolts and transmission control cable assembly.

449 kgf*cm
, 32 ft.*lbf
}

Using vernier calipers, measure the free length of the compression springs.
Minimum length:
40.5mm(1.594 in.)
HINT:
If the free length is less than the minimum, replace the compression spring.
Install the gasket.
Fully insert a new gasket to the exhaust manifold by hand.
Using a wooden block, uniformly strike the gasket so that the gasket and exhaust manifold are properly fit.
NOTICE:
Be careful with the installation direction of the gasket.
Do not reuse the gasket.
Do not damage the gasket.
To ensure a proper seal, do not use the exhaust pipe assembly front to force the gasket onto the exhaust manifold.
Install a new gasket to the exhaust pipe assembly front.
Connect the exhaust pipe assembly front to the exhaust pipe support.
Install the exhaust pipe assembly front with the 4 bolts, 2 nuts, and 2 compression springs.

Exhaust manifold side:
43 N*m{
438 kgf*cm
, 32 ft.*lbf
}
Torque:
Exhaust pipe assembly tail side:
48 N*m{
489 kgf*cm
, 35 ft.*lbf
}

For unleaded gasoline engine:
Connect the sensor connector(s).

, 32 ft.*lbf

40.5 mm (1.594 in.)

13. ADD MANUAL TRANSMISSION OIL
Park the vehicle in a level place.
Remove the transmission filler plug and gasket.

GL-4 or GL-5

SAE 75W-90

Install the transmission filler plug and a new gasket.
Torque:
37 N*m{
377 kgf*cm
, 27 ft.*lbf
}

Click here
1. INSTALL REAR ENGINE MOUNTING INSULATOR ASSEMBLY
Install the rear engine mounting insulator assembly with the 4 bolts.
Torque:
29 N*m{
296 kgf*cm
, 21 ft.*lbf
}
2. INSTALL MANUAL TRANSMISSION UNIT ASSEMBLY
Install the manual transmission unit assembly with the 9 bolts.
Torque:
72 N*m{
729 kgf*cm
, 53 ft.*lbf
}
HINT:
The A bolts in the illustration tighten the control cable bracket together.
The B bolts in the illustration tighten the rear end plate together.
Bolt C in the illustration tightens the harness clamp bracket together.
Install the transmission unit assembly to the frame with the bolt, nut, and 2 washers.
Torque:
98 N*m{
999 kgf*cm
, 72 ft.*lbf
}
NOTICE:
Insert the bolt from the left side of the vehicle.
Tighten the nut while holding the bolt.
3. INSTALL STARTER ASSEMBLY (for 2.0kW Type)
Install the starter with the bolt and 2 nuts.
Torque:
68 N*m{
693 kgf*cm
, 50 ft.*lbf
}
Connect the wire harness to terminal 30 and install the nut.
Torque:
9.8 N*m{
100 kgf*cm
, 87 in.*lbf
}
Close the terminal cap.
Connect the terminal 50 connector to the starter assembly.
for Wide body:
Install the ground cable with the bolt.
Torque:
25 N*m{
250 kgf*cm
, 18 ft.*lbf
}
4. INSTALL STARTER ASSEMBLY (for 2.7 kW Type)
Install the starter with the bolt and 2 nuts.
Torque:
68 N*m{
693 kgf*cm
, 50 ft.*lbf
}
Connect the wire harness to terminal 30 and install the nut.
Torque:
21 N*m{
215 kgf*cm
, 16 ft.*lbf
}
Close the terminal cap.
Connect the terminal 50 connector to the starter assembly.
for Wide Body:
Install the wire ground cable with the bolt.
Torque:
25 N*m{
250 kgf*cm
, 18 ft.*lbf
}
5. INSTALL CLUTCH RELEASE CYLINDER ASSEMBLY
Install the clutch release cylinder with the 2 bolts.
Torque:
12 N*m{
120 kgf*cm
, 9 ft.*lbf
}
6. INSTALL WIRE HARNESS
Connect the 2 connectors and clamps.
Install the wire harness clamp to the manual transmission.
Install the ground cable with the 2 bolts.
Torque:
13 N*m{
130 kgf*cm
, 10 ft.*lbf
}
7. INSTALL TRANSMISSION CONTROL CABLE ASSEMBLY
Install 2 new clips to the transmission control cable bracket No.1.
Install the transmission control cable assembly to the transmission control cable bracket No.1.
NOTICE:
Be sure that A claws of the clips are firmly engaged into the bracket grooves.
Be sure the cable is set in the clip with both B claws erected to prevent slippage of the cable in the opposite direction.
Align the matchmarks on the control cable assembly and the outer lever.
Install the transmission control cable assembly to the outer levers with the 2 nuts.
Torque:
37 N*m{
377 kgf*cm
, 27 ft.*lbf
}
8. INSTALL PROPELLER SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Long Wheelbase)
Remove the SST from the extension housing.
Install the propeller shaft assembly in the extension housing.
Align the matchmarks on the propeller shaft flange and differential flange.
Install the propeller shaft assembly with the 4 nuts, 4 bolts and 4 washers.
Torque:
74 N*m{
755 kgf*cm
, 54 ft.*lbf
}
9. INSTALL PROPELLER WITH CENTER BEARING SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Super Long Wheelbase)
Remove the SST from the extension housing.
Install the propeller with center bearing shaft assembly in the extension housing.
Install the center support bearing assembly No.1, and temporarily tighten the 2 bolts.
Align the matchmarks on the propeller shaft flange and differential flange.
Install the propeller shaft assembly with the 4 nuts, 4 bolts and 4 washers.
Torque:
74 N*m{
755 kgf*cm
, 54 ft.*lbf
}
Check that the center line of the bracket is at right angles to the shaft axial direction.
Adjust the center support bearing assembly No.1.
HINT:
With the vehicle unladen, adjust the center support bearing No.1 to maintain the angles, as shown.
In the same conditions, check the center line in the axial direction. Adjust the bearing if necessary.
The center bearing center line and center bearing housing center line must be adjusted to within -1.0 to 1.0 mm (-0.0394 to 0.0394 in.) of each other in the vehicle's longitudinal direction with the vehicle unladen.
Tighten the 2 bolts.
Torque:
36 N*m{
369 kgf*cm
, 27 ft.*lbf
}
10. INSTALL EXHAUST PIPE ASSEMBLY FRONT (for Long Wheelbase)
Inspect the compression spring.
Using vernier calipers, measure the free length of the compression springs.
Minimum length:
40.5mm (1.594 in.)
HINT:
If the free length is less than the minimum, replace the compression spring.
Install the gasket.
Fully insert a new gasket to the exhaust manifold by hand.
Using a wooden block, uniformly strike the gasket so that the gasket and exhaust manifold are properly fit.
NOTICE:
Be careful with the installation direction of the gasket.
Do not reuse the gasket.
Do not damage the gasket.
To ensure a proper seal, do not use the exhaust pipe assembly front to force the gasket onto the front exhaust manifold.
Connect the exhaust pipe support, and install the exhaust pipe assembly front with the 4 bolts, 2 compression springs and 2 nuts.
Torque:
exhaust manifold side:
43 N*m{
438 kgf*cm
, 32 ft.*lbf
}
exhaust pipe assembly front side:
48 N*m{
489 kgf*cm
, 35 ft.*lbf
}
NOTICE:
After installation, check that the clearance is almost same at any point between the flanges of the exhaust manifold and exhaust pipe assembly front.
11. INSTALL EXHAUST PIPE ASSEMBLY FRONT (for Super Long Wheelbase)
Inspect the compression spring.
Using vernier calipers, measure the free length of the compression springs.
Minimum length:
40.5mm(1.594 in.)
HINT:
If the free length is less than the minimum, replace the compression spring.
Install the gasket.
Fully insert a new gasket to the exhaust manifold by hand.
Using a wooden block, uniformly strike the gasket so that the gasket and exhaust manifold are properly fit.
NOTICE:
Be careful with the installation direction of the gasket.
Do not reuse the gasket.
Do not damage the gasket.
To ensure a proper seal, do not use the exhaust pipe assembly front to force the gasket onto the front exhaust manifold.
Connect the exhaust pipe support, and install the exhaust pipe assembly front and a new gasket with the 4 bolts, 2 compression springs and 2nuts.
Torque:
Exhaust manifold side:
43 N*m{
438 kgf*cm
, 32 ft.*lbf
}
Exhaust pipe assembly center side:
48 N*m{
489 kgf*cm
, 35 ft.*lbf
}
NOTICE:
After installation, check that the clearance is almost same at any point between the flanges of the exhaust manifold and exhaust pipe assembly front .
12. ADD MANUAL TRANSMISSION OIL
Park the vehicle in a level place.
Remove the transmission filler plug and gasket.
Check that the oil surface is within 5 mm (0.20 in.) below the lowest point of the transmission filler plug opening.
Oil grade:
GL-4 or GL-5
Viscosity:
SAE 75W-90
Capacity:
2.6 liters (2.7 US qts, 2.3 lmp.qts)
NOTICE:
Problems may occur when the oil level is too high or too low.
After replacing the oil, drive the vehicle and check the oil level again.
Check for oil leakage if the oil level is low.
Install the transmission filler plug and a new gasket.
Torque:
37 N*m{
377 kgf*cm
, 27 ft.*lbf
}
13. CONNECT CABLE TO NEGATIVE BATTERY TERMINAL
14. CHECK FOR EXHAUST GAS LEAKS
15. PERFORM INITIALIZATION
Some systems need initialization after reconnecting the cable to the negative battery terminal. (
Click here
)

### MANUAL TRANSMISSION ASSEMBLY (for 2KD-FTV) > REMOVAL

MANUAL TRANSMISSION ASSEMBLY (for 2KD-FTV) > REMOVAL
for Preparation
Click here
1. DISCONNECT CABLE FROM NEGATIVE BATTERY TERMINAL
2. DRAIN MANUAL TRANSMISSION OIL
Remove the filler plug and gasket.
Remove the drain plug and gasket, and drain the oil.
Install the drain plug with a new gasket.
Torque:
37 N*m{
377 kgf*cm
, 27 ft.*lbf
}
3. REMOVE EXHAUST PIPE ASSEMBLY FRONT (for Long Wheelbase)
Remove the 4 bolts,  2 nuts and 2 compression springs. 2 gasket and exhaust pipe assembly front.
Disconnect the exhaust pipe support, and remove the exhaust pipe assembly front and 2 gaskets.
4. REMOVE EXHAUST PIPE ASSEMBLY FRONT (for Super Long Wheelbase)
Remove the 4 bolts,  2 nuts, 2 compression springs. exhaust pipe assembly front and 2 gaskets.
Disconnect the exhaust pipe support, and remove the exhaust pipe assembly front and 2 gaskets.
5. REMOVE PROPELLER SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Long Wheelbase)
Put matchmarks on both flanges.
Remove the 4 nuts, bolts and washers.
HINT:
If the flange connection is hard to separate, temporarily tighten one nut only and evenly tap the flange with a brass bar and hammer to separate the propeller shaft assembly from the differential companion flange.
Remove the propeller shaft assembly.
Insert SST in the transmission to prevent oil leakage.
NOTICE:
Do not damage the oil seal.
Use the following SST for the automatic transmission
SST
09325-40010
Use the following SST for the manual transmission
SST
09325-20010
6. REMOVE PROPELLER WITH CENTER BEARING SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Super Long Wheelbase)
Put matchmarks on both flanges.
Remove the 4 nuts, bolts and washers.
HINT:
If the flange connection is hard to separate, temporarily tighten one nut only and evenly tap the flange with a brass bar and hammer to separate the propeller with center bearing shaft assembly from the differential companion flange.
Remove the 2 bolts and center support bearing assembly No.1.
Remove the propeller with center bearing shaft assembly.
Insert SST in the transmission to prevent oil leakage.
NOTICE:
Do not damage the oil seal.
Use the following SST for the automatic transmission.
SST
09325-40010
Use the following SST for the manual transmission.
SST
09325-20010
7. SEPARATE TRANSMISSION CONTROL CABLE ASSEMBLY
Put matchmarks on the control cable assembly and the outer lever.
Remove the 2 nuts and separate the transmission control cable from the outer lever.
Using a screwdriver, disengage the claws of the 2 clips.
Remove the transmission control cable and 2 clips from the transmission control cable bracket No.1.
8. DISCONNECT WIRE HARNESS
Disconnect the 2 connectors and clamps.
Separate the wire harness clamp from the manual transmission.
Remove the 2 bolts and separate the ground cable.
9. SEPARATE CLUTCH RELEASE CYLINDER ASSEMBLY
Remove the 2 bolts and separate the clutch release cylinder
10. REMOVE STARTER ASSEMBLY (for 2.0kW Type)
for Wide Body:
Remove the bolt, then remove the ground cable.
Open the terminal cap.
Remove the nut and disconnect the wire harness from terminal 30.
Disconnect the terminal 50 connector from the starter assembly.
Remove the bolt and 2 nuts, then remove the starter.
11. REMOVE STARTER ASSEMBLY (for 2.7 kW Type)
for Wide Body:
Remove the bolt, then disconnect the ground cable.
Open the terminal cap.
Remove the nut and disconnect the wire harness from terminal 30.
Disconnect the terminal 50 connector from the starter assembly.
Remove the bolt and 2 nuts, then remove the starter.
12. REMOVE MANUAL TRANSMISSION UNIT ASSEMBLY
Support the manual transmission unit with a transmission jack.
Remove the bolt, nut, and 2 washers, and then separate the transmission unit from the frame.
Remove the 9 bolts, manual transmission unit, control cable bracket No.1, rear end plate, and cylinder block insulator.
HINT:
The A bolts in the illustration tighten the control cable bracket together.
The B bolts in the illustration tighten the rear end plate together.
Bolt C in the illustration tightens the harness clamp bracket together.
13. REMOVE EXTENSION HOUSING DYNAMIC(MTM) DAMPER (WITH DYNAMIC DAMPER)
Remove the 4 bolts and extension housing dynamic (MTM) damper.
14. REMOVE REAR ENGINE MOUNTING INSULATOR ASSEMBLY
Remove the 4 bolts and rear engine mounting insulator assembly.

20. REMOVE REAR ENGINE MOUNTING INSULATOR ASSEMBLY

### CLUTCH PEDAL > ADJUSTMENT

CLUTCH PEDAL > ADJUSTMENT
for Preparation
Click here
1. INSPECT AND ADJUST CLUTCH PEDAL HEIGHT
Turn back the floor carpet.
Check that the pedal height is correct.
Pedal height from floor:
LHD
RHD
157.3 to 167.3 mm (6.193 to 6.587 in.)
160.5 to 170.5 mm (6.319 to 6.713 in.)
Loosen the lock nut and turn the stopper bolt until the correct height is obtained.
Tighten the lock nut.
Torque:
26 N*m{
260 kgf*cm
, 19 ft.*lbf
}
2. INSPECT CLUTCH PEDAL FREE PLAY AND PUSH ROD PLAY
Check that pedal free play and push rod play are correct.
Depress the pedal until clutch resistance begins to be felt.
Pedal free play:
5.0 to 15.0 mm (0.197 to 0.591 in.)
Gently depress the pedal until resistance begins to increase a little.
Push rod play at pedal top:
1.0 to 5.0 mm (0.039 to 0.197 in.)
Adjust the pedal free play and push rod play.
Loosen the lock nut and turn the push rod until correct free play and push rod play are obtained.
Tighten the lock nut.
Torque:
12 N*m{
120 kgf*cm
, 9 ft.*lbf
}
After adjusting the pedal free play, check the pedal height.
3. INSPECT CLUTCH RELEASE POINT
Check the clutch release point.
Pull the parking brake lever and install wheel stoppers.
Start the engine and run at idle.
Without depressing the clutch pedal, slowly move the shift lever into reverse until the gears contact.
Gradually depress the clutch pedal and measure the stroke distance from the point that the gear noise stops (release point) up to the full stroke end position.
Standard distance:
25 mm (0.98 in.) or more (from pedal stroke end position to release point)
Pedal stroke:
150 mm (5.906 in.)
If the distance is not as specified, perform the following operations.
Check pedal height.
Check push rod play and pedal free play.
Bleed the clutch line.
Check the clutch cover and disc.

### CLUTCH PEDAL > INSTALLATION

CLUTCH PEDAL > INSTALLATION
for Preparation
Click here
1. INSTALL CLUTCH PEDAL SPRING HOLDER
Apply MP grease to the inside of a new clutch pedal spring holder.
Install the clutch pedal spring holder.
2. INSTALL CLUTCH PEDAL PAD
Install the clutch pedal pad to the clutch pedal.
3. INSTALL CLUTCH PEDAL NO.1 CUSHION
Using needle-nose pliers, install the clutch pedal No.1 cushion to the clutch pedal.
4. INSTALL CLUTCH PEDAL SHAFT COLLAR
Apply MP grease to the inner, outer and end surfaces of 2 new pedal bushings.
Install the clutch pedal shaft collar and 2 pedal bushings to the clutch pedal.
5. INSTALL CLUTCH PEDAL SUB-ASSEMBLY
Align the matchmarks on the clutch pedal and clutch pedal support.
Install the clutch pedal to the clutch pedal support with the pedal shaft, washer, and nut.
Torque:
34 N*m{
350 kgf*cm
, 25 ft.*lbf
}
6. INSTALL TURNOVER SPRING SEAT COMPRESSION SPRING
Apply MP grease to the sliding portion of the spring.
Install the turn over spring seat compression spring.
7. INSTALL CLUTCH PEDAL SPRING (2KD-FTV ENGINE TYPE)
Apply MP grease No.2 to the sliding portion of the spring.
Install the clutch pedal spring.
NOTICE:
Be sure to install the spring with its end facing upward.
Install a new E-ring.
8. INSTALL CLUTCH PEDAL SUPPORT SUB-ASSEMBLY
Aligning the clip (clutch pedal support side) with the hole of the bracket on the vehicle, install the clutch pedal support.
NOTICE:
Make sure that the clip (clutch pedal support side) is securely engaged in the hole of the bracket on the vehicle.
Install the clutch pedal support with the bolt.
Torque:
31 N*m{
316 kgf*cm
, 23 ft.*lbf
}
Apply MP grease to the sliding portions of the push rod clevis and clutch pedal.
Install the push rod clevis to the cutout of the pedal from the right side of the vehicle and push it downward.
NOTICE:
Check that the push rod cannot be turned 30° or more in order to confirm that the clevis is securely engaged in the pedal.
9. INSTALL CLUTCH MASTER CYLINDER ASSEMBLY
Install the clutch master cylinder with the 2 nuts.
Torque:
14 N*m{
145 kgf*cm
, 10 ft.*lbf
}
10. INSPECT AND ADJUST CLUTCH PEDAL HEIGHT
(
Click here
)
11. INSTALL AIR DUCT NO.1 (for RHD)
12. INSTALL WASHER TANK AND PUMP ASSEMBLY (for LHD)
13. INSTALL INSTRUMENT PANEL FINISH PANEL LOWER CENTER
Engage the 8 claws and install the instrument panel finish panel lower center.
14. INSTALL SHIFTING HOLE COVER ASSEMBLY
Manual Transmission:
Engage the 6 claws and install the shifting hole cover assembly.
Automatic Transmission:
Engage the 8 claws and install the sifting hole cover assembly.
15. INSTALL SHIFT LEVER KNOB
16. INSTALL PARKING BRAKE HOLE COVER
Engage the 6 claws and install the parking brake hole cover.
17. INSTALL INSTRUMENT PANEL UNDER COVER SUB-ASSEMBLY NO.1
Engage the 3 claws.
Install the instrument panel No.1 under cover sub-assembly with the 2 clips.
18. INSTALL INSTRUMENT PANEL FINISH PANEL LOWER
Engage the 4 clips (B).
Install the instrument panel finish panel lower with the 2 clips (A).
19. CONNECT BATTERY NEGATIVE CABLE
20. PERFORM INITIALIZATION
Some systems need initialization when disconnecting the cable from the negative battery terminal. (
Click here
)

### CLUTCH PEDAL > REMOVAL

CLUTCH PEDAL > REMOVAL
for Preparation
Click here
1. DISCONNECT CABLE FROM NEGATIVE BATTERY TERMINAL
2. REMOVE INSTRUMENT PANEL FINISH PANEL LOWER
Using a clip remover, remove the 2 clips (A).
Disengage the 4 clips (B).
Disconnect the connector.
Push the positions indicated by the arrows in the illustration to separate the fuel lid lock control cable and bonnet (hood) control cable assembly from the panel.
Remove the instrument panel finish lower.
3. REMOVE INSTRUMENT PANEL UNDER COVER SUB-ASSEMBLY NO.1
Using a clip remover, remove the 2 clips
Disengage the 3 claws and remove the instrument panel No.1 under cover sub-assembly.
4. REMOVE PARKING BRAKE HOLE COVER
Disengage the 6 claws and remove the parking brake hole cover.
5. REMOVE SHIFT LEVER KNOB
Turn the shift lever knob in the direction indicated by the arrow and remove it.
6. REMOVE SHIFTING HOLE COVER ASSEMBLY
Manual Transmission:
Disengage the 6 claws and remove the shifting hole cover assembly.
Automatic Transmission:
Disengage the 8 claws and remove the shifting hole cover assembly.
7. REMOVE INSTRUMENT PANEL FINISH PANEL LOWER CENTER
Disengage the 8 claws and remove the instrument panel finish panel lower center.
8. REMOVE WASHER TANK AND PUMP ASSEMBLY (for LHD)
9. REMOVE AIR DUCT NO.1 (for RHD)
Remove the clip.
Release the 2 claws and remove the air duct No.1.
10. SEPARATE CLUTCH MASTER CYLINDER ASSEMBLY
Remove the 2 nuts and separate the clutch master cylinder from the clutch pedal support.
11. REMOVE CLUTCH PEDAL SUPPORT SUB-ASSEMBLY
Push the push rod clevis upward and release it toward the right side of the vehicle.
Remove the bolt and clutch pedal support.
12. REMOVE CLUTCH PEDAL SPRING (2KD-FTV ENGINE TYPE)
Using a screwdriver, remove the E-ring.
Remove the clutch pedal spring.
13. REMOVE TURNOVER SPRING SEAT COMPRESSION SPRING
Mount the clutch pedal in a soft jaw vise.
While the clutch pedal is fully depressed, remove the compression spring.
14. REMOVE CLUTCH PEDAL SUB-ASSEMBLY
Put matchmarks on the clutch pedal support.
Remove the pedal shaft, nut, washer, and clutch pedal from the clutch pedal support.
15. REMOVE CLUTCH PEDAL SHAFT COLLAR
Remove the 2 pedal bushings and pedal shaft collar from the clutch pedal.
16. REMOVE CLUTCH PEDAL NO.1 CUSHION
Remove the clutch pedal No.1 cushion.
17. REMOVE CLUTCH PEDAL PAD
Remove the clutch pedal pad from the clutch pedal.
18. REMOVE CLUTCH PEDAL SPRING HOLDER
Remove the clutch pedal spring holder from the clutch pedal support.

### REAR DIFFERENTIAL CARRIER ASSEMBLY > INSTALLATION

REAR DIFFERENTIAL CARRIER ASSEMBLY > INSTALLATION
for Preparation
Click here
1. INSTALL REAR DIFFERENTIAL CARRIER GASKET
Install a new differential carrier gasket to the rear axle housing assembly.
2. INSTALL REAR DIFFERENTIAL CARRIER ASSEMBLY
Clean the contact surfaces of the differential carrier assembly and the rear axle housing assembly.
Install the differential carrier assembly with the 10 nuts and washers.
Torque:
25 N*m{
255 kgf*cm
, 18 ft.*lbf
}
3. INSTALL LOAD SENSING BRACKET
Install the load sensing bracket with the 2 nuts.
Torque:
13 N*m{
133 kgf*cm
, 10 ft.*lbf
}
4. INSTALL REAR AXLE HOUSING DRAIN PLUG
Install the drain plug with a new gasket.
Torque:
49 N*m{
500 kgf*cm
, 36 ft.*lbf
}
5. INSTALL PROPELLER SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Super Long Wheelbase)
Remove the SST from the extension housing.
Install the propeller with center bearing shaft assembly in the extension housing.
Install the center support bearing assembly No.1, and temporarily tighten the 2 bolts.
Align the matchmarks on the propeller shaft flange and differential flange.
Install the propeller shaft assembly with the 4 nuts, 4 bolts and 4 washers.
Torque:
74 N*m{
755 kgf*cm
, 54 ft.*lbf
}
Check that the center line of the bracket is at right angles to the shaft axial direction.
Adjust the center support bearing assembly No.1.
HINT:
With the vehicle unladen, adjust the center support bearing No.1 to maintain the angles, as shown.
In the same conditions, check the center line in the axial direction. Adjust the bearing if necessary.
The center bearing center line and center bearing housing center line must be adjusted to within -1.0 to 1.0 mm (-0.0394 to 0.0394 in.) of each other in the vehicle's longitudinal direction with the vehicle unladen.
Tighten the 2 bolts.
Torque:
36 N*m{
369 kgf*cm
, 27 ft.*lbf
}
6. INSTALL PROPELLER SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Long Wheelbase)
Remove the SST from the extension housing.
Install the propeller shaft assembly in the extension housing.
Align the matchmarks on the propeller shaft flange and differential flange.
Install the propeller shaft assembly with the 4 nuts, 4 bolts and 4 washers.
Torque:
74 N*m{
755 kgf*cm
, 54 ft.*lbf
}
7. INSTALL REAR AXLE SHAFT LH OIL SEAL
Using SST and a hammer, install a new rear axle shaft oil seal.
SST
09554-22010
Seal installation depth:
34.5 to 35.5 mm (1.358 to 1.398 in.)
NOTICE:
Do not drive the oil seal in deeper than the specified range or an oil leak will occur.
Do not tilt the oil seal during installation.
Text in Illustration
*1
Rear Axle Housing Assembly
*2
Rear Axle Shaft Oil Seal
*a
Seal installation depth
Apply MP grease to the oil seal lip.
8. INSTALL REAR AXLE SHAFT RH OIL SEAL
HINT:
Installation procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
9. INSTALL BEARING RETAINER O-RINGS
Apply MP grease to the bearing retainer O-ring.
Install the bearing retainer O-ring to the rear axle shaft housing.
10. INSTALL REAR AXLE SHAFT WITH BACKING PLATE LH
Install the rear axle shaft with backing plate to the rear axle shaft housing with the 4 nuts.
Torque:
65 N*m{
663 kgf*cm
, 48 ft.*lbf
}
NOTICE:
Be careful not to damage the rear axle shaft oil seal.
Be careful not to damage the skid control rotor rear.
11. REMOVE REAR AXLE SHAFT WITH BACKING PLATE RH
HINT:
Installation procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
12. INSTALL SPEED SENSOR REAR LH (w/ ABS)
Install the new speed sensor O-ring to the rear speed sensor.
Install the rear speed sensor to the rear axle shaft housing with the bolt.
Torque:
8.0 N*m{
82 kgf*cm
, 71 in.*lbf
}
NOTICE:
Be careful not to damage the rear speed sensor.
Prevent foreign matter from adhering to the speed sensor.
Do not twist the speed sensor wire when installing the speed sensor.
13. INSTALL SPEED SENSOR REAR RH (w/ ABS)
HINT:
Installation procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
14. INSTALL REAR WHEEL BRAKE CYLINDER ASSEMBLY LH
Install the wheel brake cylinder assembly with the 2 bolts.
Torque:
9.5 N*m{
97 kgf*cm
, 84 in.*lbf
}
Using SST, connect the brake tube.
SST
09023-00101
Torque:
15 N*m{
155 kgf*cm
, 11 ft.*lbf
}
15. INSTALL REAR WHEEL BRAKE CYLINDER ASSEMBLY RH
HINT:
Installation procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
16. APPLY HIGH TEMPERATURE GREASE
Apply high temperature grease to the shoe attached surface of the backing plate.
17. CONNECT PARKING BRAKE CABLE ASSEMBLY NO. 3
Install the parking brake cable assembly No.3 to the rear brake backing plate with the 2 bolts.
Torque:
8.0 N*m{
82 kgf*cm
, 71 in.*lbf
}
18. CONNECT PARKING BRAKE CABLE ASSEMBLY NO. 2
HINT:
Installation procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
19. INSTALL PARKING BRAKE SHOE STRUT SET LH
Apply the high temperature grease to the adjusting bolt.
Install the tension spring to the show strut set.
20. INSTALL PARKING BRAKE SHOE STRUT SET RH
HINT:
Installation procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
21. INSTALL REAR BRAKE SHOES
Using pliers, install the rear brake shoe, shoe strut set, rear cushion lever and shoe lever with a new C-washer.
Connect the parking brake cable No.3 to the front brake shoe.
Using SST, install the rear brake shoe, pin, shoe hold down spring and shoe hold down cup.
SST
09718-00010
22. INSTALL FRONT BRAKE SHOES
Install the return spring to each brake shoe.
Using SST, install the front brake shoe, pin, shoe hold down spring and shoe hold down cup.
SST
09718-00010
Install the brake shoe lower strut.
NOTICE:
Make sure that the shoe lower strut and brake rear cushion lever are securely engaged.
Using needle-nose pliers, install the tension spring.
23. CONNECT PARKING BRAKE SHOE STRUT SET LH
Using SST, install the upper side tension spring.
SST
09703-30011
24. CONNECT PARKING BRAKE SHOE STRUT SET RH
HINT:
Installation procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
25. INSTALL AUTOMATIC ADJUST LEVER LH
Install the automatic adjust lever and tension spring.
NOTICE:
Make sure to install the automatic adjust lever between the groove of the shoe strut set and brake shoe.
26. INSTALL AUTOMATIC ADJUST LEVER RH
HINT:
Installation procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
27. INSPECT REAR DRUM BRAKE
Check the each part is installed properly.
NOTICE:
There should be no oil or grease adhering to the friction surfaces of the shoe lining and drum.
If they are not installed correctly, reinstall them as shown in the illustration.
28. INSTALL REAR AXLE BRAKE DRUM GASKETS
Install the new brake drum gasket to the rear axle shaft.
29. INSTALL REAR BRAKE DRUM SUB-ASSEMBLIES
30. ADJUST REAR DRUM BRAKE SHOE CLEARANCE
Using a screwdriver from a service hole, turn the adjuster to expand the shoes so that the brake shoes touch the brake drum.
Using another screwdriver, push up the automatic adjust lever and turn the adjuster to contract the shoes so that the brake shoe does not touch the brake drum. Then turn the adjuster another 180 degrees to further contract the shoes.
Install the hole plug.
31. FILL BRAKE FLUID
Fluid:
SAE J1704 or FMVSS No. 116 DOT3 or equivalent
32. BLEED BRAKE LINE
Connect the vinyl tube to the bleeder plug.
Depress the brake pedal several times and loosen the bleeder plug with the pedal held down.
At the point where the fluid stops coming out, tighten the bleeder plug and release the brake pedal.
Repeat this procedure until the air in the brake fluid is completely bled out.
Tighten the bleeder plug.
Front bleeder plug:
Torque:
10.8 N*m{
110 kgf*cm
, 8 ft.*lbf
}
Rear bleeder plug:
Torque:
11.0 N*m{
112 kgf*cm
, 8 ft.*lbf
}
Repeat the above procedure to bleed the air out of the brake line for each wheel.
33. INSPECT BRAKE FLUID LEVEL
Check the fluid level and add fluid if necessary.
Fluid:
SAE J1704 or FMVSS No.116 DOT3 or equivalent
34. FILL DIFFERENTIAL OIL
Remove the differential filler plug and gasket.
Fill with oil.
Oil grade:
Hypoid gear oil API GL-5 or equivalent
Recommended oil viscosity
Above -18°C (0°F)
SAE 90
Below -18°C (0°F)
SAE 80W or 80W-90
Check the oil level.
Install the differential filler plug with a new gasket.
Torque:
49 N*m{
500 kgf*cm
, 36 ft.*lbf
}
NOTICE:
After replacing the oil, recheck the oil level after driving.
35. INSPECT AND ADJUST DIFFERENTIAL OIL
Stop the vehicle on a level place.
Remove the differential filler plug and gasket.
Check that the oil surface is within 5 mm (0.20 in.) of the lowest position of the inner surface of the differential filler plug opening.
NOTICE:
Excessively large or small amounts of oil may cause trouble.
After replacing oil, drive the vehicle and check the oil level.
HINT:
If necessary, fill the rear differential carrier with hypoid gear oil.
Check for oil leakage when the oil level is low.
Install the differential filler plug and a new gasket.
Torque:
49 N*m{
500 kgf*cm
, 36 ft.*lbf
}
36. INSTALL REAR WHEELS
Torque:
100 N*m{
1,020 kgf*cm
, 74 ft.*lbf
}
37. INSPECT PARKING BRAKE CONTROL HANDLE TRAVEL
Pull firmly on the parking brake control handle.
Release the parking brake lock, and return the parking brake control handle to its off position.
Slowly pull the parking brake control handle all the way up, and count the number of clicks.
Parking brake control handle travel:
10 to 16 clicks at 200 N (20 kgf, 44 lbf)
HINT:
If the number of clicks falls outside of the specified range, release the parking brake lock and adjust it.
If there are fewer clicks than the specified value, loosen the parking brake wire adjustment nut an the lock nut. With the parking brake cable loosened, adjust the clearance between the brake drum and lining.
38. ADJUST PARKING BRAKE CONTROL HANDLE TRAVEL
Lift the vehicle
Depress the parking brake handle. Hold the parking brake adjusting nut using a wrench, and loosen the lock nut.
Turn the parking brake adjusting nut until the parking brake handle travel meets the above specification.
Parking brake control handle travel:
10 to 16 clicks at 200 N (20 kgf, 44 lbf)
Count the number of clicks after depressing and releasing the parking brake control handle 3 or 4 times.
Check whether the parking brake drags or not.
When operating the parking brake control handle, check that the parking brake indicator light comes on.
Standard:
Brake warning light always comes on at the first click.
Hold the parking brake adjusting nut using a wrench, and tighten the lock nut.
Torque:
14.5 N*m{
148 kgf*cm
, 11 ft.*lbf
}
Lower the vehicle.
39. ABS SPEED SENSOR SIGNAL
(
Click here
)

### REAR DIFFERENTIAL CARRIER ASSEMBLY > REMOVAL

REAR DIFFERENTIAL CARRIER ASSEMBLY > REMOVAL
for Preparation
Click here
1. REMOVE REAR WHEELS
2. DRAIN DIFFERENTIAL OIL
Remove the filler plug and gasket.
Remove the drain plug and gasket, and drain the oil.
3. DRAIN BRAKE FLUID
4. REMOVE REAR BRAKE DRUM SUB-ASSEMBLIES
Release the parking brake lever, and remove the brake drum.
HINT:
If the brake drum cannot be removed easily, perform the following steps.
Remove the hole plug and insert a screwdriver through the hole in the backing plate, and hold the automatic adjusting lever away from the adjuster.
Using another screwdriver, contract the brake shoe adjuster by turning the adjusting wheel.
5. REMOVE REAR AXLE BRAKE DRUM GASKETS
6. REMOVE AUTOMATIC ADJUST LEVER LH
Remove the automatic adjust lever and the tension spring.
7. REMOVE AUTOMATIC ADJUST LEVER RH
HINT:
Removal procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
8. SEPARATE PARKING BRAKE SHOE STRUT SET LH
Using SST, remove the upper side tension spring from the brake shoe.
SST
09703-30011
9. SEPARATE PARKING BRAKE SHOE STRUT SET RH
HINT:
Removal procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
10. REMOVE FRONT BRAKE SHOES
Using a needle-nose pliers, remove the anchor side tension spring.
Using SST, remove the cup, shoe hold-down sprig and  pin.
SST
09718-00010
Remove the parking brake shoe lower strut.
Separate the brake shoe return spring, and remove the front brake shoe.
11. REMOVE REAR BRAKE SHOES
Using SST, remove the cup, shoe hold-down sprig and pin.
SST
09718-00010
Disconnect the parking brake cable No.3 and remove the rear brake shoe.
12. REMOVE PARKING BRAKE SHOE STRUT SET LH
Using a screwdriver, remove the C-washer, brake shoe lever, rear cushion lever and brake shoe strut set from the brake shoe.
Remove the adjusting bolt and tension spring from the brake shoe strut set.
13. REMOVE PARKING BRAKE SHOE STRUT SET RH
HINT:
Removal procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
14. SEPARATE PARKING BRAKE CABLE ASSEMBLY NO. 3
Remove the 2 bolts and separate the parking brake cable assembly No.3 from the rear brake backing plate.
15. SEPARATE PARKING BRAKE CABLE ASSEMBLY NO. 2
HINT:
Removal procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
16. REMOVE REAR WHEEL BRAKE CYLINDER ASSEMBLY LH
Using SST, disconnect the brake tube, use a container to catch brake fluid.
SST
09023-00101
Remove the 2 bolts and wheel cylinder.
17. REMOVE REAR WHEEL BRAKE CYLINDER ASSEMBLY RH
HINT:
Removal procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
18. SEPARATE SPEED SENSOR REAR LH (w/ ABS)
Remove the bolt and separate the rear speed sensor.
NOTICE:
Prevent foreign matter from adhering to the speed sensor.
Be careful not to damage the speed sensor.
Remove the O-ring from the rear speed sensor.
19. SEPARATE SPEED SENSOR REAR RH (w/ ABS)
HINT:
Removal procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
20. REMOVE REAR AXLE SHAFT WITH BACKING PLATE LH
Remove the 4 nuts and rear axle shaft with backing plate.
NOTICE:
Be careful not to damage the rear axle shaft oil seal.
Be careful not to damage the skid control rotor rear.
21. REMOVE REAR AXLE SHAFT WITH BACKING PLATE RH
HINT:
Removal procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
22. REMOVE BEARING RETAINER O-RINGS
Remove the bearing retainer O-ring from the rear axle housing assembly.
23. REMOVE REAR AXLE SHAFT LH OIL SEAL
Using SST, remove the rear axle shaft oil seal from the rear axle housing assembly.
SST
09308-00010
24. REMOVE REAR AXLE SHAFT RH OIL SEAL
HINT:
Removal procedure of the RH side is the same as that of the LH side.
25. REMOVE PROPELLER SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Super Long Wheelbase)
Put matchmarks on both flanges.
Remove the 4 nuts, bolts and washers.
HINT:
If the flange connection is hard to separate, temporarily tighten one nut only and evenly tap the flange with a brass bar and hammer to separate the propeller with center bearing shaft assembly from the differential companion flange.
Remove the 2 bolts and center support bearing assembly No.1.
Remove the propeller with center bearing shaft assembly.
Insert SST in the transmission to prevent oil leakage.
NOTICE:
Do not damage the oil seal.
Use the following SST for the automatic transmission.
SST
09325-40010
Use the following SST for the manual transmission.
SST
09325-20010
26. REMOVE PROPELLER SHAFT ASSEMBLY (for Long Wheelbase)
Put matchmarks on both flanges.
Remove the 4 nuts, bolts and washers.
HINT:
If the flange connection is hard to separate, temporarily tighten one nut only and evenly tap the flange with a brass bar and hammer to separate the propeller shaft assembly from the differential companion flange.
Remove the propeller shaft assembly.
Insert SST in the transmission to prevent oil leakage.
NOTICE:
Do not damage the oil seal.
Use the following SST for the automatic transmission
SST
09325-40010
Use the following SST for the manual transmission
SST
09325-20010
27. DISCONNECT LOAD SENSING BRACKET
Remove the 2 nuts and load sensing bracket.
28. REMOVE REAR DIFFERENTIAL CARRIER ASSEMBLY
Support the differential carrier assembly with a jack.
NOTICE:
Do not drop the differential carrier assembly
Remove the 10 nuts, washers and differential carrier assembly.
NOTICE:
Do not damage the installation surface when removing the differential carrier assembly.
The remaining oil may leak out when removing the differential carrier assembly.
29. REMOVE REAR DIFFERENTIAL CARRIER GASKET

### REAR DIFFERENTIAL CARRIER ASSEMBLY > DISASSEMBLY

REAR DIFFERENTIAL CARRIER ASSEMBLY > DISASSEMBLY
for Preparation
Click here
1. FIX REAR DIFFERENTIAL CARRIER ASSEMBLY
Set the differential carrier to an overhaul stand, etc., as shown in the illustration.
2. INSPECT RUNOUT OF REAR DRIVE PINION COMPANION FLANGE SUB-ASSEMBLY
Using a dial indicator, measure the runout of the companion flange vertically and horizontally.
Maximum runout:
0.09 mm (0.0035 in.)
If the runout is greater than the maximum value, replace the companion flange sub-assembly.
3. INSPECT RUNOUT OF DIFFERENTIAL RING GEAR
Set the dial indicator perpendicular to the end of the ring gear face.
Rotate the ring gear and measure the runout.
Maximum runout:
0.07 mm (0.0028 in.)
If the runout exceeds the specified maximum value, remove the ring gear and check the runout of the differential case.
4. INSPECT DIFFERENTIAL RING GEAR BACKLASH
Set the dial indicator perpendicular to the end of the ring gear face.
While holding the rear drive pinion companion flange rear, rotate the ring gear and measure the backlash.
Backlash:
0.13 to 0.18 mm (0.0051 to 0.0071 in.)
If the backlash is not within the specified range, adjust the preload or repair as necessary.
5. INSPECT DIFFERENTIAL DRIVE PINION PRELOAD
Using a socket wrench (30 mm) and torque wrench, measure the preload using the backlash of the drive pinion and ring gear.
Preload (at starting):
0.56 to 0.85 N*m (6.0 to 9.0 kgf*cm, 5.0 to 8.0 in.*lbf)
6. INSPECT TOTAL PRELOAD
Using a socket wrench (30 mm) and torque wrench, measure the preload with the teeth of the drive pinion and ring gear in contact.
Total preload (at starting):
Drive pinion preload plus 0.39 to 0.59 N*m (4.0 to 6.0 kgf*cm, 3.5 to 5.2 in.*lbf)
7. REMOVE REAR DRIVE PINION NUT
Using SST and a hammer, release the staked part of the drive pinion nut.
SST
09930-00010
NOTICE:
Be sure to use SST with the tapered surface facing the shaft.
Do not grind the tip of the SST with a grinder etc.
Completely loosen the staked part of the nut when removing it.
Do not damage the threads of the drive pinion.
Using SST, hold the flange.
SST
09330-00021
Using a socket wrench (30 mm), remove the drive pinion nut.
8. REMOVE REAR DRIVE PINION COMPANION FLANGE SUB-ASSEMBLY
Using SST, remove the companion flange.
SST
09950-30012
(09951-03010, 09953-03010, 09954-03010, 09955-03030, 09956-03040)
NOTICE:
Apply grease to the threads and tip of the SST center bolt before use.
9. REMOVE REAR DIFFERENTIAL DUST DEFLECTOR
HINT:
Perform this procedure only when the dust deflector is damaged.
Using SST and a press, remove the dust deflector.
SST
09950-60010
(09951-00380)
09950-70010
(09951-07150)
09950-00020
10. REMOVE REAR DIFFERENTIAL CARRIER OIL SEAL
Using SST, remove the oil seal from the differential carrier.
SST
09308-10010
NOTICE:
Apply grease to the threads and tip of the SST center bolt before use.
11. REMOVE REAR DIFFERENTIAL DRIVE PINION OIL SLINGER
12. REMOVE REAR DRIVE PINION FRONT TAPERED ROLLER BEARING
Using SST, remove the inner race of the rear drive pinion front tapered roller bearing from the drive pinion.
SST
09556-22010
NOTICE:
Apply grease to the threads and tip of the SST center bolt before use.
13. REMOVE REAR DIFFERENTIAL BEARING ADJUSTING NUT LOCK
Remove the 2 bolts and 2 bearing adjusting nut locks.
14. REMOVE DIFFERENTIAL CASE ASSEMBLY
Put matchmarks on either set of the bearing cap and differential carrier.
Remove the 4 bolts and 2 bearing caps.
NOTICE:
Do not swap a bearing cap and carrier as they are manufactured as a set.
Remove the 2 rear differential bearing adjusting nuts.
Remove the differential case assembly and case bearing outer races LH and RH from the differential carrier.
Put identification marks on the case bearing outer races and bearing adjusting nuts to distinguish between the RH side and LH side.
15. REMOVE DIFFERENTIAL DRIVE PINION
Remove the drive pinion and bearing spacer from the differential carrier.
16. REMOVE REAR DRIVE PINION REAR TAPERED ROLLER BEARING
Using SST and a press, remove the inner race of the rear drive pinion rear tapered roller bearing from the drive pinion.
SST
09950-00020
HINT:
If either the drive pinion or ring gear is damaged, replace both as a set.
Remove the drive pinion plate washer from the drive pinion.
17. REMOVE REAR DRIVE PINION FRONT TAPERED ROLLER BEARING
Using a brass bar and a hammer, remove the outer race of the rear drive pinion front tapered roller bearing from the differential carrier.
18. REMOVE DIFFERENTIAL OIL STORAGE RING
Using a brass bar and a hammer, remove the oil storage ring from the differential carrier.
19. REMOVE REAR DRIVE PINION REAR TAPERED ROLLER BEARING
Using a brass bar and a hammer, remove the outer race of the rear drive pinion rear tapered roller bearing from the differential carrier.
20. REMOVE DIFFERENTIAL RING GEAR
Hold the differential case in a vise between aluminum plates.
NOTICE:
Do not overtighten the vise.
Put matchmarks on the ring gear and differential case.
Using a screwdriver and a hammer, release the 5 lock plates.
Remove the 10 ring gear set bolts and 5 lock plates.
Using a plastic hammer, tap on the ring gear to separate it from the differential case.
21. INSPECT RUNOUT OF DIFFERENTIAL CASE ASSEMBLY
HINT:
Perform this procedure only when the runout of the differential ring gear exceeds the specified maximum value.
Install the case bearing outer races LH and RH to the case bearing inner races LH and RH respectively.
NOTICE:
Be sure to install the bearing outer races in each correct position.
Install the differential case to the differential carrier.
Align the matchmarks on the bearing cap and differential carrier.
Install the right and left bearing caps with the 4 bolts.
Torque:
85 N*m{
870 kgf*cm
, 63 ft.*lbf
}
Using a dial indicator, measure the differential case runout.
Maximum case runout:
0.04 mm (0.0016 in.)
If the runout is greater than the maximum value, replace the differential case assembly with a new one.
Remove the 4 bolts, right and left bearing caps and differential case.
22. REMOVE REAR DIFFERENTIAL CASE BEARING
HINT:
Perform this procedure only when replacing the case bearing or differential case.
Hold the differential case in a vise between aluminum plates.
NOTICE:
Do not overtighten the vise.
Using SST, remove the case bearing inner race LH and RH from the differential case.
SST
09950-40011
(09951-04020, 09952-04010, 09953-04030, 09954-04010, 09955-04061, 09957-04010, 09958-04011)
09950-60010
(09951-00360)
NOTICE:
Do not deform the bearing cage if the bearing is to be reused.
Hook the SST claw from the dent of the differential case to the bearing inner race.
Apply grease to the threads and tip of the SST center bolt before use.
23. REMOVE REAR DIFFERENTIAL PINION SHAFT PIN
Using a pin punch (5 mm) and a hammer, remove the straight pin.
Remove the differential pinion shaft. [A]
Remove the 2 differential pinions. [B]
Remove the 2 differential pinion thrust washers. [C]
Remove the 2 side gears. [D]
Remove the 2 side gear thrust No.1 washers. [E]
24. INSPECT DIFFERENTIAL PINION AND SIDE GEAR
Check that there is no damage to the differential pinion gear and side gear. If the differential pinion gear and/or side gear is damaged, replace them with new ones.
25. INSPECT DIFFERENTIAL CASE
Check that there is no damage to the differential case. If the differential case is damaged, replace it.
